questions.text: Electric flux $\phi$ is related with linear charge density $\lambda$ and surface charge density $\sigma$ as $\phi = \alpha \lambda + \beta \sigma$ where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are of appropriate dimensions. Dimension of $\left(\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\right)$ is
questions.solution: $\alpha \lambda \equiv \beta \sigma \Rightarrow \frac{\beta}{\alpha} = \frac{\lambda}{\sigma} = \frac{Q/L}{Q/L^2} = L \equiv \text{Displacement}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The ratio of electric force to gravitational force between two particles having charges $q_1, q_2$ and masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ respectively is (where symbols have their usual meanings)
questions.solution:
$F_g = \frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2}$, $F_e = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$
$\frac{F_e}{F_g} = \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 G m_1 m_2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Match the column appropriately regarding thermodynamic process.
Column-I:
(P) When volume change is zero
(Q) When pressure is constant
(R) When no heat is exchanged
(S) Work done by the gas is equal to heat given to the gas
Column-II:
(i) $\Delta W = 0$
(ii) $\Delta Q = 0$
(iii) Isobaric
(iv) Isothermal
questions.solution:
Volume change is zero $\rightarrow$ Isochoric $\rightarrow \Delta W = 0$
When pressure is constant $\rightarrow$ Isobaric
No heat exchange $\rightarrow$ Adiabatic $\rightarrow \Delta Q = 0$
Heat given = Work done $\Rightarrow \Delta U = 0 \Rightarrow \Delta T = 0$ (Isothermal)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In given DC circuit, find current for $R = 12\ \Omega$ in steady state.
questions.solution:
In steady state, inductor acts as a short circuit (zero resistance).
$i = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{12}{12} = 1\text{ A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Hot water is less viscous than cold water.
Statement-II : Surface tension of soap bubble is more than that of a drop of water.
options: (1) Statement-I is true and statement-II true
(2) Statement-I is true and statement-II false
(3) Statement-I is false and statement-II true
(4) Statement-I is false and statement-II false
questions.solution: Viscosity of liquids decreases with increase in temperature, so Statement-I is true. Surface tension of soap solution is less than pure water, so Statement-II is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The key shown in the circuit is closed at $t = 0$. Choose the incorrect option regarding the conditions at $t = 0$.
options: (1) Current in the circuit is zero
(2) Voltage across the capacitor is minimum
(3) Current in the circuit is maximum
questions.solution: Immediately after closing the key the capacitor acts as a short circuit (path of zero resistance). Hence, current is maximum at $t = 0$, so option (1) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A uniform solid sphere of mass $m$ rolls down from rest to achieve speed $v_1$ on an inclined plane of $30^\circ$. Sphere achieves speed $v_2$ on an inclined plane of $45^\circ$ when released from same height then $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2}$ is (assume no slipping)
questions.solution:
$|\Delta U| = |\Delta K| \Rightarrow mgh = \frac{1}{2}(\gamma + 1)mv^2$ where $\gamma = \frac{2}{5}$
Since $h$ is the same, $v$ doesn't depend on angle of inclination $\theta$, so $\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2} = 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Find the equation of magnetic field for the given equation of electric field (for EM wave):
$\vec{E} = E_0(4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})\cos(\omega t - kz)$
questions.solution:
Phase difference between magnetic and electric field is zero.
$|\vec{B}| = \frac{5 E_0}{C}$
Direction of wave propagation is along $+\hat{k} = \hat{E} \times \hat{B}$.
Thus, unit vector along $\vec{B}$ is $\frac{3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}}{5}$.
So $\vec{B} = \frac{E_0}{C}(3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\cos(\omega t - kz)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Self-inductance depends on :
questions.solution: $L = \mu_r \mu_0 n^2 V$ where $\mu_r$ is relative permeability of the medium and $V$ is volume (geometry).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
For the circuit shown below:
(A) Current in ammeter is 2 A
(B) Net resistance is $8\ \Omega$
(C) Voltage across BC is 4 V
(D) Current through diode is 1 A
Choose the correct option.
questions.solution:
$R_{eq} = 6\ \Omega$
$i = \frac{12}{6} = 2\text{ A}$
$i_{AB} = 1\text{ A}$
$V_{BC} = 4\text{ V}$
Hence, statements (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the time period of a cube of side length 10 cm and mass 10 g oscillating in water. (density of water $= 10^3\text{ kg/m}^3$ and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution:
$a = -\omega^2 x = -\frac{\Delta B}{m} = -\frac{(0.1)^2 \times x \times 10^3 \times 10}{10^{-2}} = -10^4 x$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Adiabatic constant of a gas is $\frac{3}{2}$. If volume of gas initially at 0°C is reduced to one fourth of the original volume then new temperature is
questions.solution:
$T V^{\gamma-1} = \text{constant}$
$273 V^{1/2} = T \left(\frac{V}{4}\right)^{1/2}$
$T = 2 \times 273 = 546\text{ K}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two objects are equal distances from sphere of radius $R$ & refractive index $\mu$ such that the image of one object forms on other object. Find the object distance from the surface of sphere.
questions.solution:
After first refraction, the ray must become parallel to the principal axis ($v = \infty$).
$\frac{\mu}{v} - \frac{1}{-u} = \frac{\mu - 1}{R} \Rightarrow 0 + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{\mu - 1}{R} \Rightarrow u = \frac{R}{\mu - 1}$

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a radioactive decay, decay constant of element $A_2$ is 3 times that of element $A_1$. Find the ratio of nuclei of element 1 to element 2 after one half life of $A_2$ (Assume initial number of nuclei are same for both elements)
questions.solution:
$N_1 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_1 t}, N_2 = N_0 e^{-\lambda_2 t}$
$\frac{N_1}{N_2} = e^{(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1)t}$
Since $t = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda_2} = \frac{\ln 2}{3\lambda_1}$,
$\frac{N_1}{N_2} = e^{2\lambda_1 \cdot \frac{\ln 2}{3\lambda_1}} = e^{\frac{2}{3}\ln 2} = 2^{2/3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through potential $V$ is $\lambda$. If the potential is increased to $4V$, the new de Broglie wavelength becomes:
questions.solution: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$. When potential is $4V$, wavelength becomes $\frac{\lambda}{\sqrt{4}} = \frac{\lambda}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a photoelectric experiment, stopping potential for incident light of frequency $\nu$ is $V_1$ and for frequency $2\nu$ is $V_2$. Find the work function of the metal.
questions.solution:
$eV_1 = h
u - \Phi \Rightarrow 2eV_1 = 2h
u - 2\Phi$
$eV_2 = 2h
u - \Phi$
Subtracting gives $eV_2 - 2eV_1 = \Phi \Rightarrow \Phi = e(V_2 - 2V_1)$.

questions.text: From a uniform circular disc of radius 20 cm a circular portion of radius 5 cm is removed. The shift in the position of centre of mass (in cm) is
questions.solution: $X_{com} = \frac{\frac{M}{16} \times 15}{M - \frac{M}{16}} = \frac{15}{15} = 1\text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A bullet of kinetic energy of 125 J strikes a lead block where temperature rises by 50°C. If specific heat of lead is 0.1 J/g-°C then mass of lead block is (Assume half of kinetic energy of bullet is converted to heat) $m$ gram then $2m$ is
questions.solution: $Q = ms\Delta T \Rightarrow \frac{125}{2} = m \times 0.1 \times 50 \Rightarrow m = 12.5\text{ g} \Rightarrow 2m = 25$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A wire of resistance $20\ \Omega$ is bent into a circle. Find the effective resistance between two diametrically opposite points in ohms.
questions.solution: The wire is divided into two equal semicircular branches of $10\ \Omega$ each in parallel. $R_{eq} = \frac{10 \times 10}{10 + 10} = 5\ \Omega$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is thrown with speed $20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ with horizontal. Find its maximum height in meters. ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution: $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = \frac{400 \times (1/4)}{20} = 5\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In YDSE, slit separation is $0.5\text{ mm}$ and fringe width observed on a screen $1\text{ m}$ away is $1.2\text{ mm}$. Find the wavelength of light used in nm.
questions.solution: $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d} \Rightarrow 1.2 \times 10^{-3} = \frac{\lambda \times 1}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} \Rightarrow \lambda = 600\text{ nm}$.

questions.text:
Which of the following compound can react with Hinsberg reagent?

(C) Methyl amine

questions.solution: Primary and secondary amines react with Hinsberg reagent. Aniline (primary), Methyl amine (primary), and N-phenyl aniline (secondary) will react.

questions.text: Among the following, the most stable carbanion is
questions.solution: Cyclopentadienyl anion is aromatic ($6\pi$ electrons) and hence most stable among the options.

questions.solution: $[Ma_3 b_3]$ type complex compound shows facial-meridional (fac-mer) isomerism where $a, b$ are monodentate ligands.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following pair of ions have same colour?
questions.solution: $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ = Blue and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ = Blue.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following does not belong to the same period in the modern periodic table?
questions.solution: Os, Ir, Pt belong to $6^{\text{th}}$ period, while Pd belongs to $5^{\text{th}}$ period of modern periodic table.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Identify the product formed in the following reaction:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO} + \text{HCHO (excess)} \xrightarrow[\text{Reflux}]{\text{OH}^-} \dots$
questions.solution: Propanal undergoes aldol condensation with excess HCHO in presence of $\text{OH}^-$ ions to 2,2-dihydroxymethylpropanal which further undergoes Cannizzaro reaction to give 2,2-dihydroxymethylpropan-1-ol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Incorrect statement among the following is
options: (1) SO2 act as oxidising agent but not reducing agent
(3) PF5 exists but NF5 does not
(4) PH3 has lower proton affinity than NH3
questions.solution: $\text{SO}_2$ acts as an oxidising as well as a reducing agent because sulphur is in $+4$ oxidation state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions starting from 1-methyl-4-nitrobenzene:
(i) $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$
(ii) $\text{Sn/HCl}$
(iii) $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl } (0-5^\circ\text{C})$
(iv) $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$
Find the molecular mass of the final product (A) formed in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: Final product (A) is 3-bromotoluene ($\text{C}_7\text{H}_7\text{Br}$). Molecular mass $= 7(12) + 7(1) + 80 = 171\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the Column I with Column II and choose the correct option.
Column I:
A. $\text{BF}_3$
B. $\text{CCl}_4, \text{CO}_2$
C. $\text{PCl}_5, \text{BrF}_5$
D. $\text{NO}$
Column II:
(i) Odd $e^-$ species
(ii) Expanded octet
(iii) Complete octet
(iv) Electron deficient
questions.solution:
$\text{BF}_3 \rightarrow$ Electron deficient ($6 e^-$)
$\text{CCl}_4, \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow$ Complete octet ($8 e^-$)
$\text{PCl}_5, \text{BrF}_5 \rightarrow$ Expanded octet
$\text{NO} \rightarrow$ Odd electron species

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match column-I with column-II:
Column-I:
(A) $2\text{Ph-Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Na/D.E}}$
(B) $\text{Ph-N}_2\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{CuCl/HCl}}$
(C) $\text{Ph-Cl} + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{Na/D.E}}$
(D) $\text{CH}_3\text{-Cl} + \text{AgF} \rightarrow$
Column-II:
(P) Sandmeyer reaction
(Q) Fittig reaction
(R) Wurtz-Fittig reaction
(S) Swarts reaction
questions.solution:
Matching named reactions:
$2\text{Ph-Cl} \rightarrow \text{Ph-Ph}$ (Fittig)
$\text{Ph-N}_2\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{Ph-Cl}$ (Sandmeyer)
$\text{Ph-Cl} + \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{Ph-CH}_3$ (Wurtz-Fittig)
$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{AgF} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{F}$ (Swarts)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is forming an octahedral complex with spin only magnetic moment 3.83 BM. The correct electronic configuration for cobalt in the complex is?
questions.solution:
$\mu = 3.83\text{ BM} \Rightarrow n = 3$ unpaired electrons.
$\text{Co}^{2+} = 3d^7$. For a weak field ligand, configuration is $t_{2g}^5 e_g^2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement-I : During Lassaigne's test, covalent compound is converted to ionic compound.
Statement-II : $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]$ gives Prussian blue colour on reaction with $\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$.
options: (1) S-I is correct, S-II is incorrect
(2) S-I is incorrect, S-II is correct
(3) Both S-I and S-II are correct
(4) Both S-I and S-II are incorrect
questions.solution:
Both statements are correct.
$3\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6] + 2\text{Fe}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3 \rightarrow \text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]_3 + 6\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4$ (Prussian blue).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
$\text{A}(g) \rightarrow 2\text{B}(g)$
For the given reaction, initial pressure was 0.6 atm and rate constant is $4.606 \times 10^{-2}\text{ sec}^{-1}$. Find the total pressure at 100 sec.
questions.solution:
$kt = 2.303 \log \frac{P_0}{P_0 - p}$
$4.606 \times 10^{-2} \times 100 = 2.303 \log \frac{0.6}{0.6 - p} \Rightarrow p = 0.594\text{ atm}$
Total pressure $= 0.6 + p = 0.6 + 0.594 = 1.194\text{ atm}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
Statement-I: Fructose does not contain aldehyde group but it gives Tollen's test.
Statement-II: In disaccharides, if the reducing groups are bonded, these are non-reducing sugar e.g., sucrose. If these functional groups are free then they are reducing sugar e.g. maltose and lactose.
options: (2) Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect
(3) Statement-I is incorrect, Statement-II is correct
(4) Statement-I and Statement-II both are incorrect
questions.solution: Fructose tautomerises to glucose/mannose in basic medium and reduces Tollen's reagent. Disaccharides with linked anomeric carbons are non-reducing.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For a sample of Hydrogen atom, the wavelength observed is 656 nm during a transition. The transition and corresponding series in hydrogen spectrum will be
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R_H Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$
For $\lambda = 656\text{ nm}$, $n_1 = 2$ and $n_2 = 3$, corresponding to Balmer series $3 \rightarrow 2$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following molecules has zero dipole moment?
questions.solution: $\text{XeF}_4$ has square planar geometry with symmetric distribution of bond dipoles and lone pairs, resulting in zero net dipole moment.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is a diamagnetic complex?
questions.solution: In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $3d^6$ with strong field ligand $\text{CN}^-$. All 6 electrons pair up in $t_{2g}$ orbitals ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$), so it is diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in strongly acidic medium gives:
questions.solution: Electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in strongly acidic medium initially forms phenylhydroxylamine, which rearranges to $p$-aminophenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following standard reduction potentials corresponds to the strongest reducing agent?
questions.solution: More negative standard electrode potential indicates greater tendency to get oxidized, hence a stronger reducing agent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which polymer is formed by condensation polymerization?
questions.solution: Nylon-6,6 is formed by condensation polymerization of hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: If 2 g phenol is allowed to react with $\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. How much $\text{Br}_2$ (in g) will be required to produce 2, 4, 6 tribromophenol (Rounded off to nearest integer).
questions.solution:
3 moles $\text{Br}_2$ react with 1 mole phenol.
$\text{Br}_2\text{ required} = \frac{2}{94} \times 160 \times 3 = 10.2\text{ g} \approx 10\text{ g}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: When $10^{21}$ molecules are removed from $x$ mg of $\text{CO}_2(g)$, then $2.4 \times 10^{-3}$ moles of $\text{CO}_2$ are left. Calculate the value of $x$. [Take $N_A = 6 \times 10^{23}$]
questions.solution:
Moles removed $= \frac{10^{21}}{6 \times 10^{23}} = 1.67 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$
Total moles $= (2.4 + 1.67) \times 10^{-3} = 4.07 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}$
Mass $= 4.07 \times 10^{-3} \times 44\text{ g} = 179\text{ mg}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following Latimer diagram:
$\text{FeO}_4^{2-} \xrightarrow{2.0\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^{3+} \xrightarrow{0.8\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^{2+} \xrightarrow{-0.5\text{ V}} \text{Fe}^0$
Find $E^0_{\text{FeO}_4^{2-}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}$ (rounded to nearest integer).
questions.solution: $-4 F E^0 = -3 F (2) + (-1 F)(0.8) \Rightarrow -4 E^0 = -6.8 \Rightarrow E^0 = 1.7\text{ V} \approx 2\text{ V}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the given values :
$\Delta H = 55\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, $\Delta S = 175\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, $T = 25^\circ\text{C}$.
Calculate the value of Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G$) in $\text{J mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S = 55000 - 298 \times 175 = 55000 - 52150 = 2850\text{ J mol}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In estimation of sulphur by Carius method, 160 g of organic compound gives 466 g of Barium sulphate. % of sulphur in the organic compound is _____.
questions.solution:
233 g $\text{BaSO}_4$ contains 32 g sulphur.
466 g $\text{BaSO}_4$ contains 64 g sulphur.
$\%\text{ sulphur} = \frac{64}{160} \times 100 = 40\%$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: How many words can be formed from the word "DAUGHTER" such that any vowels are not together
questions.solution:
Total arrangements without restriction $= 8! = 40320$.
Arrangements with all vowels together $= 6! \times 3! = 720 \times 6 = 4320$.
Required $= 8! - 6! \times 3! = 36000$.

questions.text: Value of $\cos^{-1}\left[\frac{12}{13}\cos x + \frac{5}{13}\sin x\right]$ for $x \in \left[\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]$ is
questions.solution:
Let $\tan \alpha = \frac{5}{12} \Rightarrow \cos \alpha = \frac{12}{13}, \sin \alpha = \frac{5}{13}$.
$\cos^{-1}[\cos(x - \alpha)] = x - \alpha = x - \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{12}\right)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation defined on set $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, then how many ordered pairs are added to $R = \{(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3)\}$ so that it becomes equivalence relation?
questions.solution:
To make $R$ an equivalence relation on $A$, we need reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.
Pairs to add: $(1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 4), (2, 1), (3, 2), (3, 1), (1, 3)$. Total $= 7$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sum of all rational terms in the expansion of $\left(1 + 2^{1/3} + 3^{1/2}\right)^6$ is
questions.solution:
General term: $\frac{6!}{\alpha! \beta! \gamma!} 1^\alpha (2^{1/3})^\beta (3^{1/2})^\gamma$.
For rational terms, $3 \mid \beta$ and $2 \mid \gamma$ with $\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 6$.
Sum of rational terms $= 27 + 45 + 135 + 27 + 40 + 360 + 4 = 638$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\left|\frac{z}{z + i}\right| = 2$ represents a circle with centre $P$ then distance of $P$ from $D(1, 5)$ is (where $i = \sqrt{-1}$)
questions.solution:
$|z| = 2|z + i| \Rightarrow x^2 + y^2 = 4(x^2 + (y+1)^2) \Rightarrow 3x^2 + 3y^2 + 8y + 4 = 0$.
Center $P = \left(0, -\frac{4}{3}\right)$.
$PD = \sqrt{(1 - 0)^2 + \left(5 + \frac{4}{3}\right)^2} = \sqrt{1 + \frac{361}{9}} = \frac{\sqrt{370}}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider the set $S = \{1, 2, 3, \dots, 1000\}$. Then the number of arithmetic progression that can be formed using elements of set $S$ such that first term is 1 and last term is 1000 is
questions.solution:
$T_n = 1 + (n-1)d = 1000 \Rightarrow (n-1)d = 999 = 27 \times 37 = 3^3 \times 37^1$.
Number of divisors of $999 = (3+1)(1+1) = 8$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A$ and $B$ are non-singular commutative matrices. Then $A\left[(\text{adj } A^{-1}) (\text{adj}(B^{-1}))\right]^{-1} B$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\text{adj}(A^{-1}) = \frac{A}{|A|}$
$A[(\text{adj } A^{-1})(\text{adj } B^{-1})]^{-1} B = A \left[\frac{A}{|A|} \frac{B}{|B|}\right]^{-1} B = A [A^{-1} B^{-1}] |A||B| B = |A||B| I_n$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the curve satisfying the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{6 - 2e^{2x}y}{1 + e^{2x}}$ passes through $(0, 0)$ and $(\ln 2, k)$, then $k$ is
questions.solution:
$\frac{dy}{dx} + \left(\frac{2e^{2x}}{1 + e^{2x}}\right) y = \frac{6}{1 + e^{2x}}$
I.F. $= 1 + e^{2x}$
$y(1 + e^{2x}) = 6x + c$. Passes through $(0, 0) \Rightarrow c = 0$.
For $x = \ln 2$: $y(1 + 4) = 6\ln 2 \Rightarrow k = \frac{6}{5}\ln 2$.

questions.solution:
Rewrite integral: $I = \int \frac{dx}{(x - 1)^2 \left(\frac{x + 15}{x - 1}\right)^{15/13}}$.
Let $y = \frac{x + 15}{x - 1} \Rightarrow dy = \frac{-16}{(x-1)^2} dx$.
$I = -\frac{1}{16} \int y^{-15/13} dy = \frac{13}{32} y^{-2/13} + C = \frac{13}{32} \left(\frac{x - 1}{x + 15}\right)^{2/13} + C$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the system of equations $x + y + z = 6$, $x + 2y + 3z = 10$, $x + 2y + az = b$ has infinitely many solutions, then $a + b$ is equal to:
questions.solution: For infinite solutions, row operations give $a = 3$ and $b = 10$. Thus $a + b = 13$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The distance of point $(1, 2, 3)$ from the plane $x - y + z = 5$ measured parallel to the line $\frac{x}{1} = \frac{y}{2} = \frac{z}{2}$ is:
questions.solution:
A point on the line is $(1+r, 2+2r, 3+2r)$. Substituting into $x - y + z = 5 \Rightarrow (1+r) - (2+2r) + (3+2r) = 5 \Rightarrow r = 3$.
Distance $= \sqrt{r^2 + (2r)^2 + (2r)^2} = 3r = 9$? Wait, if normalized direction vector is used, distance $= r \times 1 = 3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the area bounded by the curve $y = x^2$ and the line $y = 4$.
questions.solution: Area $= 2 \int_0^2 (4 - x^2) dx = 2 \left[4x - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = 2 \left(8 - \frac{8}{3}\right) = \frac{32}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $f(x) = |x - 1| + |x - 2|$, then $f(x)$ is not differentiable at:
questions.solution: $f(x)$ has sharp corners at $x = 1$ and $x = 2$, so it is non-differentiable at $x = 1, 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $y = (\sin x)^{\tan x}$, then $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$ is:
questions.solution: $\ln y = \tan x \ln(\sin x)$. Differentiating gives $\frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx} = \sec^2 x \ln(\sin x) + 1$. At $x = \pi/4$, $\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 \cdot (2 \ln(1/\sqrt{2}) + 1) = 1 - \ln 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$, where $f(x) = \frac{2}{x}[\sin(k_1+1)x + \sin(k_2+1)x]$ for $x < 0$, $f(0) = 4$, and $f(x) = \frac{2}{x}\log\left[\frac{k_2 x + 1}{k_1 x + 1}\right]$ for $x > 0$. Then $k_1^2 + k_2^2$ is
questions.solution:
$\,\lim_{x \to 0^-} f(x) = 2(2 + k_1 + k_2) = 4 \Rightarrow k_1 + k_2 = 0$.
$\lim_{x \to 0^+} f(x) = 2(k_2 - k_1) = 4 \Rightarrow k_2 - k_1 = 2$.
Solving gives $k_1 = -1, k_2 = 1 \Rightarrow k_1^2 + k_2^2 = 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
If for the system of linear equations having infinite solutions:
$(\lambda - 4)x + (\lambda - 2)y + \lambda z = 0$
$2x + 3y + 5z = 0$
$x + 2y + 6z = 0$
then $\lambda^2 + \lambda$ is
questions.solution:
Determinant of coefficient matrix $= 0 \Rightarrow 2\lambda - 18 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 9$.
$\lambda^2 + \lambda = 81 + 9 = 90$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the equation $a(b - c)x^2 + b(c - a)x + c(a - b) = 0$ has equal roots and if $a + c = 5$ and $b = \frac{16}{5}$, then the value of $a^2 + c^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Root is 1, so both roots are 1.
Product of roots $= 1 \Rightarrow \frac{c(a-b)}{a(b-c)} = 1 \Rightarrow 2ac = b(a+c) = \frac{16}{5}(5) = 16$.
$a^2 + c^2 = (a+c)^2 - 2ac = 25 - 16 = 9$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The area of larger portion enclosed by curves $y = |x - 1|$ and $x^2 + y^2 = 25$ is equal to $\frac{1}{4}(\alpha \pi + \beta)$ sq. units (where $\alpha, \beta$ are natural numbers), then $\alpha + \beta$ equals to
questions.solution:
Intersection points are $(-3, 4)$ and $(4, 3)$.
$\text{Area} = 25\pi - \int_{-3}^4 \left(\sqrt{25 - x^2} - |x - 1|\right) dx = \frac{1}{4}(75\pi + 2)$.
$\alpha = 75, \beta = 2 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 77$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = \frac{\pi}{k}$, then find the value of $k$.
questions.solution: $\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = [\sin^{-1} x]_0^1 = \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow k = 2$.
